subject: Re: Production latency incident — proposed SLO attribution & evidence playbook
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@helix-medical.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Increased tail latency on private deployment 2027-05-09 — request for SLA review

Hi Vanessa,

We observed several customer-facing degradation events yesterday (05/09) where inference requests to our private VPC cluster experienced p95 spikes from ~120ms to 950ms for ~90 minutes. Our on-call traced the issue to a network flapping event between our edge peering and the data-center router; however we wanted to open this formally to discuss whether this counts against Redwood's SLO for the private deployment.

We are also preparing a procurement request to add more capacity, but before that we need clarity on whether Helix is eligible for SLA credit or an SLO carve-out given the apparent customer-controlled networking failure. Can you confirm what evidence you need and a timeline for review?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering — Helix Medical Systems
ops@helix-medical.com

Attachments: request-log-snippet.txt (sample errors),

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@helix-medical.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency on private deployment 2027-05-09 — request for SLA review

Hi Samira — thanks for the quick note and the log snippet. Sorry you hit that window.

Quick summary of where we stand: because this is a Private deployment with the VPC owned/peered by Helix, the default shared-responsibility model attributes customer-managed network faults to Helix. That said, we do have a formal attribution process so that we can objectively determine whether the incident should impact Redwood's uptime/latency SLOs for your contract.

What we need from you to start the attribution review (minimal set):
- 1 hour of packet capture (pcap) spanning the incident window and 15 minutes before/after
- Router/switch syslogs for the same window (timestamps in UTC)
- Inference gateway access logs (timestamped request latencies) from your side and Redwood's front-door logs for cross-correlation
- Confirmation of any maintenance events or config changes on the peering/edge devices

I've attached a short "evidence checklist" to guide collection. Once we receive those, we'll run a deterministic correlation (timestamps, seq numbers, and TCP RTO patterns) and share an attribution report within 5 business days. If the root cause is on the Helix-managed path, we would propose not to apply an SLA credit to that incident; if the correlation indicates packet loss or queuing attributable to Redwood's front-door, we will apply remedies per the contract.

As a temporary operational measure, would Helix consider enabling our lightweight observability agent (no data plane change, only metadata and timing hooks) on one gateway for 72 hours? That will reduce ambiguity for future events.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments: evidence-checklist.csv

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:10:00 -0400
Subject: FW: Helix incident — legal/contract approach

Looping in legal/tech policy context. Two quick points for the draft response to the customer: 1) keep attribution criteria objective and reproducible (avoid ad-hoc exemptions), 2) offer a pragmatic interim SLA handling approach so the customer has runway during their infra remediation.

Suggested interim handling: provide a "bounded attribution" outcome that records the incident as "mixed causality" when evidence is inconclusive and propose a proportional credit formula (e.g., credit = contract-credit * attribution_factor where attribution_factor is between 0 and 1 determined by our correlation). That prevents a binary pass/fail which customers often find frustrating.

Also recommend we offer the lightweight observability agent as an opt-in with a 30-day trial and a short data-retention policy note to address Helix's compliance team.

— Karthik

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: evidence thresholds + timeframe for Helix review

Vanessa — drafting timeline for the Helix request. My proposed internal playbook:
- Day 0 (receipt): acknowledge and request artifacts (pcap + router logs + local gateway traces)
- Day 1–2: run automated correlation job (pairwise timestamp correlation across logs, compute packet loss/RTT deltas)
- Day 3: if correlation inconclusive, kick manual packet analysis and request optional agent deployment
- Day 4–5: finalize attribution and produce a one-page report with recommended remediation and credit calculation.

Thresholds to flag Redwood responsibility:
- >1% sustained TCP packet loss between Redwood front door and customer egress for >5 minutes during the window
- RTT delta increase >300ms compared to baseline for >10 minutes and corroborated on both sides' traces
- Evidence of Redwood routing misconfiguration (BGP withdraws, AS path changes)

If none of those trigger, we mark "customer-attributed" but include mitigations and offer 30-day agent trial.

I'll prepare the slo-attribution-playbook-v1.pdf and the credit-proforma examples. We should keep language non-legal but align with contract appendix.

— Mina

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@helix-medical.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency on private deployment 2027-05-09 — proposed SLO attribution & evidence playbook

Hi Samira — following internal alignment, attached is our proposed SLO attribution playbook (PDF) and the evidence checklist. Summary of the proposal:

1) Objective criteria: we run automated correlation against the artifacts you provide. If objective triggers (packet loss, RTT delta, BGP changes) show Redwood responsibility, we accept SLA impact.

2) Mixed causality: if correlation shows both sides contributed or evidence is insufficient, we apply a proportional credit using a transparent formula (we included examples in the playbook).

3) Timelines: we aim to return a preliminary attribution within 5 business days from receipt of artifacts; final report within 10 business days if manual analysis needed.

4) Short-term mitigations: we can enable a lightweight observability agent for 72 hours to reduce future ambiguity (agent collects timing metadata only; no packet payloads).

Next steps we need from Helix: a) attach the full pcap and syslogs for 05/09 ; b) confirm any maintenance that day; c) point us to your network ops contact (ops-networking@helix-medical.com is fine).

If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute call today to walk the checklist through with your ops lead.

Thanks — we'll stand by to begin analysis once artifacts arrive.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-attribution-playbook-v1.pdf, evidence-checklist.csv
